plan.major: Real Estate and the Built Environment
plan.notes: University of Denver is on the quarter system (Fall/Winter/Spring); term_system=quarter. Official sample 4-year course plan from the 2025-2026 Undergraduate Bulletin Real Estate and the Built Environment program PDF (12 quarters). Years 1-3 are common to all students (bulletin states Total Credits: 146); Fourth Year has THREE concentration options the student selects 1 of: (1) Real Estate Finance & Investments (REFI), (2) Real Estate Development (RED), (3) Construction Management (CM) — each 40 credits with the same structure (ASEM, MGMT 3000, BUS 3800, four concentration electives, general electives). This plan encodes the shared Years 1-3 plus Concentration Option 1 (REFI) as the representative fourth year; the concentration elective slots are generic choice slots and the option-2/option-3 elective lists are documented here: RED electives — REAL 3210, REAL 3357, REAL 3367, REAL 3377, CMGT 3155, REAL 3140, REAL/CMGT 3980 or CMGT 3700; CM electives — CMGT 3100, CMGT 3120, CMGT 3155, CMGT 3480, REAL 3140, REAL/CMGT 3980 or CMGT 3700. REFI electives (select 16 cr hrs): REAL 3010, REAL 3317, REAL 3367, REAL 3369, REAL 3377, REAL 3140, REAL 3337, REAL/CMGT 3980 or CMGT 3700. Declared total 186 (146 + 40); term totals (Y1 16/16/16, Y2 18/16/16, Y3 16/16/16, Y4 16/12/12) reconcile exactly. Generic slots (business courses per footnotes 6/7/8, language/SI sequences, Common Curriculum, REBE core/concentration/elective/minor blocks, study-abroad block, general electives) encoded as choice slots exactly as the official plan lists them; no courses invented. Third Year Fall: study abroad (16 credits) OR International Course (4) plus three REBE Core/Concentration, Elective or Minor courses (4 each) — encoded as the four-slot path with the study-abroad alternative documented; both total 16. MGMT 3000 prerequisites: all Microsoft certifications and all Business Core except BUS 3800. BUS 3800 may be taken fall, winter, or spring after MGMT 3000. Footnote 1: MATH 1200 or MATH 1951 fulfills Analytical Inquiry: The Natural and Physical World. Footnote 2: ECON 1030 is required for all Business majors and fulfills half the Scientific Inquiry: Society and Culture requirement. Footnote 3: complete Language or SI: Natural and Physical World sequence; one in year 1, the other in year 2. Footnote 4: INTZ 2501 required for any student who studies abroad; may be taken any quarter within the year prior to studying abroad. Footnote 5: non-international, non-study-abroad students select an advisor-approved course for the Student International Experience Requirement; REAL 3140 can satisfy it and count as one of the four REBE concentration electives.
